title: THE TEN VIRGINS
mv: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.
mvp: ‘‘Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.’’ Matthew 25:1
assignment: Mention five (5) attributes you should not exhibit as a believer (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: A virgin is someone or something that is pure, unexplored, etc. In the parable of the ten virgins in Matthew 25, Jesus gives a staggering revelation that a virgin can be wise or foolish. These virgins came to meet the bridegroom, but their level of preparedness was different; five of them made provision for extra oil while the other five did not. Let us learn from the wise and foolish virgins and be ready for the Master’s return.
The foolish virgins had these characteristics:

i: Inability to Seize Opportunity: Meeting the bridegroom was a great opportunity, but they did not take advantage of it (Matthew 25:9-12).
Carefree: They were too relaxed in their present state of limited oil (Matthew 25:8).
Distracted: They were preoccupied with sleep; if not, they would have known when their lamps were giving warning signals of low oil (Matthew 25:5; Proverbs 6:4, 10-11).

Lacked Foresight: They were not detailed enough to know ahead of time that there could be a probability that the bridegroom could tarry in His coming, so they did not bother to have an extra oil in their baggage (Matthew 25:3).
No Thirst For Knowledge: They did not inquire from their co-virgins why they made provision for extra oil.
Prepared: They were ready for the bridegroom irrespective of all odds (Matthew 25:5-9, 10).
Informed: They had an inkling that the bridegroom could tarry in His coming (Matthew 25:4-5).
Attentive to Details: They did not forget to take extra oil for their lamps (Matthew 25:4).
At The Right Place: They never left the spot where they were waiting for the bridegroom for anything, so when He came, they entered with Him (Matthew 25:8-10).
Extra preparation: Although they also slept before the bridegroom came, their extra preparation for their lamps saved the day (Matthew 25:4-5, 10).

b.x: The Bridegroom in this parable is Jesus, and He is warning us to be ready for His return because “Heaven is a prepared place for prepared people.” Jesus said our righteousness must exceed that of the “Scribes and Pharisees” to enter Heaven (Matthew 5:20). We must be equipped by putting on the whole armour of God (Ephesians 6:11-18). Believers must remove all dross from their silver (Proverbs 25:4) and take away any sin-stained garment (Ecclesiastes 9:8). Complete obedience to God and His word in all areas of life is key (1 Samuel 15:22). To be holy as we bear the vessels of the Lord is none negotiable (Isaiah 52:11; 1 Peter 1:16). It is required that we purge ourselves daily as we watch and pray (Mark 13:33-37).
Although we do not know when Jesus will return, our business is to be ready (Matthew 24:36).
Be spotless and ready for the return of Jesus Christ.
